title: Friction that slows a slide depends on the two surfaces that touch
summary: Friction that slows a sliding object depends on the two surfaces in contact, so a rough pair and a smooth pair do not drag the same way.
body: OpenStax Physics says a sliding box slows because friction, a force from outside, acts against the motion. Kinetic friction is the force from a surface, parallel to that surface, that opposes a slide and causes the object to slow. The size of that force depends on a coefficient of friction and on the normal force. The coefficient is a constant that depends on the nature of the two surfaces. The section asks for smooth and rough surfaces as examples of that difference. An air-hockey table is the page's picture of a case where lifting the puck makes the friction very small, so the puck hardly slows. The card does not give a coefficient for any named pair of materials.
